entry_state: Participation rights allocate earnings between classes before division; dividends are allocations rather than another expense. Assumed option proceeds include future services, and assumed share settlement may change earnings as well as shares. A senior cumulative entitlement and participation cap now replace the simple proportional allocation.
exit_state: Capped participation requires recalculating ordinary attribution after each assumed share issue. A restricted ordering result survives fixed rights and independent nonnegative gross effects. Joint bonus or tax consequences can violate that additivity; a two-convertible bonus-threshold example now begins.
findings: Adding50 ordinary shares reduces the preference residual allocation and gives ordinary EPS12/17, not the frozen-numerator2/3.
The max-of-two-ratios derivation relies on the same additive gross effects in both fractions. The prose explicitly excludes dependent bonus effects from that result.
